conflicts.fact: Whether the breathing rate increase is explained by muscle ATP/oxygen demand or by fuel switching, and the direction of the causal chain
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 says the body shifts from carbohydrate to fat during prolonged exercise (RQ 1.0 to 0.7), and that the burning sensation is connected to this fuel shift. Lessons 7, 10 and 12 attribute the burning sensation to lactic acid from anaerobic respiration. Lesson 8 also claims fat 'requires MORE oxygen' so the lungs and heart work harder, and ties this to the 2-minute step-up exercise. Lesson 8's RQ framing contradicts the unit's explanation (anaerobic lactic acid) for the burning legs.

conflicts.fact: Why breathing rate increases (stimulus and causal chain)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says the rise results from increased ATP demand, so aerobic respiration consumes more O₂ and produces more CO₂. Lesson 12 gives a chain starting with muscle ATP demand and aerobic respiration, then CO₂ build-up driving increased breathing. Lesson 11 says mitochondria consuming glucose 'continuously deplete local oxygen' as the reason the body works harder. These accounts of the stimulus differ (O₂ depletion vs CO₂ build-up).

conflicts.fact: Blood vessel and heart route for oxygenated blood
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says oxygenated blood travels 'pulmonary vein → left side of heart → aorta', consistent with the anatomy. Lesson 5's Observe phase says 'lung capillaries → pulmonary veins → left side of heart → aorta → arteries'. No conflict with Lesson 6, but Lesson 6 says the oxygen 'travels air → lungs → blood → muscle cell' without the heart. This is not a contradiction.

conflicts.fact: Respiration enzyme temperature and heat discussion vs Lesson 10 'cold Kericho highlands' heat regulation; also Lesson 9 says Lesson 1 learners recorded warm skin
conflicts.versions: Lesson 9 claims learners in Lesson 1 'recorded that your body felt warmer' and felt skin become warm, but Lesson 1 only records breathing rate, pulse rate and burning legs; warmth was never observed or recorded in Lesson 1.

conflicts.fact: Number of respiratory surfaces and which ones were studied, and earthworm inclusion in the unit model
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 compares four surfaces (earthworm skin, fish gills, insect tracheae, mammalian alveoli). Lesson 3 covers three surfaces (alveoli, tilapia gills, insect tracheae) and says 'all efficient respiratory surfaces share the same four adaptations'. Lesson 11 Zone A lists four surfaces including earthworm skin.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 1 model: whole-class model vs individual naive model
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 has each learner draw an individual naive model of oxygen's pathway into muscle cells. Lesson 2 refers to 'the simple whole-class model begun in Lesson 1 (a sketch of a person with arrows showing air in and out, and rising numbers...)'. Lesson 7 says the model was 'begun in Lesson 1 and revised in Lessons 3, 5, and 6', skipping Lessons 2 and 4, while Lesson 9 says the cumulative cellular respiration diagram was first drawn in Lesson 6.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 4 attributes breathing rate, Lesson 5 attributes pulse
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 gives example learners Wanjiku (14 to 28) and Baraka (16 to 30), Lesson 5 gives Amina pulse 74 to 128, and Lesson 6 gives Achieng 16 to 34 breaths and 74 to 128 bpm. The pulse values 74 to 128 are attributed to Amina in Lesson 5 and Achieng in Lesson 6 as 'class data'.

conflicts.fact: Where the cumulative model ownership and who did the DQB 'Explained' milestone for breathing rate
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 marks 'Why does breathing rate increase during exercise?' as FULLY EXPLAINED, while Lesson 7 says the burning legs question was open since Lesson 1 and was only resolved in Lesson 7; Lesson 10 and 12 still treat the driving question as incompletely answered and Lesson 8 raises RQ as a new explanation of the burning, inconsistent with the lesson-7 resolution.
